Surah 110 (An-Nasr) is Madinan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1–3} In this noble surah there is good news, a command to His Messenger when it occurs, an allusion, and an admonition concerning what follows from that.

As for the good news, it is the glad tidings of Allah's victory for His Messenger, his conquest of Makkah, and the entry of people {into the religion of Allah in multitudes}, such that many of them become its adherents and helpers after having been its enemies. This promised thing has indeed come to pass.

As for the command after the victory and conquest have been achieved, Allah commanded His Messenger to thank Him for that, to glorify Him with His praise, and to seek His forgiveness.

As for the allusion, there are two allusions in this. The first: that victory continues for the religion and increases upon the occurrence of glorifying Allah with His praise and seeking His forgiveness by His Messenger, for this is part of gratitude, and Allah says: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]﴾. This has been realized in the time of the Rightly Guided Caliphs and after them in this Ummah. The victory of Allah continued uninterrupted until Islam reached what no other religion had reached, and entered it those who had entered no other, until the Ummah fell into opposing the command of Allah, so they were afflicted with division of word and scattering of affairs, and what happened, happened. Nevertheless, for this Ummah and this religion there is from the mercy and kindness of Allah what does not occur to the mind or pass through the imagination.

As for the second allusion, it is an indication that the term of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has drawn near and approached. Its explanation is that his lifespan is a virtuous lifespan, by which Allah swore, and it is well known that virtuous matters are concluded with seeking forgiveness, such as prayer, Hajj, and other things. So Allah's command to His Messenger to praise and seek forgiveness in this state is an indication that his term has ended; so let him prepare and make ready to meet his Lord and conclude his life with the best that he can find, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. He [ﷺ] used to interpret the Qur'an and say that in his prayer; he would often say in his bowing and prostration: "Subhanaka Allahumma Rabbana wa bihamdika, Allahumma! Ighfir li" ("Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me").
